page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7se.16xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed under the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 64 dedicated virtual CPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There are no graphics processing units included in this configuration.

For storage and connectivity, the instance contains no local storage volumes, requiring external network block storage for persistent data and operating system volumes. Networking capabilities include a baseline throughput of 16 Gbps. Public IPv4 connectivity is not included by default and must be configured separately.

From an operational perspective, the large memory density provides an efficient deployment target for workloads that demand significant RAM per core without requiring GPU acceleration or low-latency ephemeral drives. The lack of bundled local storage shifts IOPS scaling and retention entirely to attached block storage. The instance profile aligns with in-memory caching solutions, enterprise relational database systems, real-time analytics, and large enterprise application workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7se.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance engineered for enterprise workloads requiring extensive system memory. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, it features 64 dedicated vCPUs backed by a 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor. The instance provides 512.0 GB of total RAM, corresponding to an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is not present, as the system includes zero GPUs. Local storage is not provided, requiring administrators to utilize network-attached cloud disks for persistent filesystem and boot requirements. Network operations are supported by a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth profile, while complimentary public IPv4 addresses are omitted. By offering a high ratio of memory to compute cores, this instance delivers strong resource density for in-memory databases, distributed caches, enterprise application runtimes, and large-scale data processing tasks where massive RAM footprints take precedence over local ephemeral disk storage.
